clue.text: Gangster without assistance seizing crown

explanation.surface: A mobster who acts alone grabs a monarch's crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (2,6) hides a name: the answer is the famous Prohibition gangster, not a word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago crime boss of the Prohibition era, a famous example of the type.

clue.text: Brisk sailor with routine, quietly absorbed

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in and held within something else

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A sailor's daily routine goes on with quiet absorption, yet he remains brisk.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk manner is curt and sharp, which is what an abrupt manner is too.

clue.text: Group in government showing it can be complicated

indicators.note: something made complicated is tangled up, so these letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry remark that governing bodies can make matters complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is the body of senior ministers that runs a government, a group within it.

clue.text: Role involving a prank, worry for actor

indicators.note: to involve is to include or wrap in, so one word takes the others inside it

parts.note: a part is a role played on stage
a trick is a prank
to stew is to fret or worry

explanation.surface: A part in a play includes a practical joke, which worries the performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The role word is split in two, its first letter standing apart while both the prank and the worry go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick Stewart is the English stage and screen performer, known as Captain Picard and Professor X, so an example of an actor.

clue.text: Hour during pleasant recess

indicators.note: something happening during something else falls within it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant
h is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: An hour spent enjoying a nice break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a school break, but here it is an alcove in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow alcove set into a wall, which is one kind of recess.

clue.text: Direct debit cutting very large price

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing pierces it and lies inside it

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing label for very large
DD is the standard abbreviation for direct debit

explanation.surface: A bank payment slashing a hefty bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, the odds are the price offered by a bookmaker, as in a horse starting at a long price.

clue.text: Failure with information about old resentment

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
o is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A flop accompanied by details of a long-held grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offence or resentment, chiefly heard in the phrase 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Time put into search over half of area in plant

indicators.note: to put one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: a sweep is a thorough search of an area
t is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only two of its four letters, here the back pair

parts.note: the back half of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A gardener spends time combing half the bed for a particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' here means on top of, so the search with time inside sits above the half in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden flower grown for its scented blooms, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Be successful mostly on court in view

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to prosper is to do well
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A tennis player hopes to succeed while on court in full view.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a view or vista, especially a wide one seen from a high place.

clue.text: Official threat shaking strong belief

indicators.note: shaking something up throws it into disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning from authority rattles someone's deeply held conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: An article of faith is a firmly held conviction, originally a tenet of a religious creed.

clue.text: Cheat turning to automatic machine

parts.note: to rob someone is to cheat them of something

indicators.note: turning round makes the short word face the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A swindler resorting to mechanical help.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine that carries out tasks automatically, often programmed to mimic human actions.

clue.text: Convey elevation in case

parts.note: to cart is to carry or transport
a ridge is a raised strip of ground

explanation.surface: Carrying goods up a hill just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a casing holding ammunition, ink or film, so a type of case.

clue.text: Writes about river safari, initially poor

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses another

parts.note: to pen is to write
the Nile is the great African river

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A travel writer covers a Nile safari and ends up broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone penniless has no money at all, so is poor in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Popular point about English being awkward

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation wraps round a letter

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
pt is the abbreviation for point
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A well-liked point about English proves clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, clumsy or maladroit, the same as awkward in handling things.

clue.text: Go for it, needing that leg-up, keen to work

indicators.note: letters set to work are put through their paces and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Encouragement to an eager climber who needs a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the plunge is an idiom for committing boldly to a decision, just as 'go for it' urges.

clue.text: Violent behaviour almost embraced in test

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a try is a test or attempt

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not fully, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to embrace is to hug

explanation.surface: An exam where rough handling almost turns into a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggery is the brutal conduct of thugs, a fair name for violent behaviour.

clue.text: Shortage having lasting effect on urban area

parts.note: a scar is a lasting mark left by an injury or trauma
a city is a large urban area

explanation.surface: A shortage that leaves a long-term mark on a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is the condition of being in short supply, a lack or shortage of something.

clue.text: Angry protests after damage outside new buildings

indicators.note: after means coming behind, setting the order of the two parts
outside means surrounding, so one word goes round a letter

parts.note: cost as in 'what's the damage?', the price of something
n is the abbreviation for new
ructions are noisy rows or angry protests

explanation.surface: Furious demonstrations follow vandalism outside newly built homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' is informal British for the cost of something, as in 'what's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: Constructions are things that have been built, such as buildings or structures.

clue.text: Constant drama, north and south, before summit

parts.note: No, or Noh, is the classical Japanese drama
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south
the top is the summit

explanation.surface: A relentless play about a journey from north to south and up a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonstop goes on without a break, so it is constant and unceasing.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps in secure state capital

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

parts.note: safe means secure
a soldier ant is one kind of ant; 'perhaps' marks soldier as just an example

explanation.surface: A soldier stationed in a well-guarded seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks military, but it is the insect: soldier ants guard the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital city of the US state of New Mexico.

clue.text: Layers in places drilled by man

indicators.note: something drilled has a hole bored through it, with the drill inside

parts.note: to set something is to place it
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A workman boring holes through layered materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets are thin flat pieces laid on one another, like layers of rock, paper or ice.

clue.text: Some now energetic in retirement begin again

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters are read backwards
some means a part of the following words, held within them

parts.note: the run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Pensioners who suddenly feel lively decide to start afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to resume or start something over, as in renewing an attack.

clue.text: Distance after day covered by game bird

indicators.note: after means coming behind, setting the order of the parts
something covered by another is wrapped inside it

parts.note: golf is a game
d is the abbreviation for day
an inch is a short distance

explanation.surface: A day's hunting covers some ground in search of game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' runs together as a phrase, but 'game' is a sport and 'bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch is a small songbird with a bright red face and gold wing bars.

clue.text: Learner with excessive love for game

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
OTT, over the top, means excessive
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A novice who gets far too keen on a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery or a bingo-style game of chance played with numbered cards.

clue.text: Explain concern, not small, about public relations

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word wraps round the abbreviation
not tells us to leave something out

parts.note: an interest is a concern, such as a business stake
s is the abbreviation for small
PR is the abbreviation for public relations

explanation.surface: A PR agent accounts for a company's large concern.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain the meaning of something, such as a text or a dream.

clue.text: Cross island with speed

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Crossing an island at pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as a verb for travelling over the island, but it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, the adjective sense of cross.

clue.text: Chatters, getting power in voice back

indicators.note: back means the result is read in the opposite direction
in places one letter inside the word

parts.note: to voice is to say
p is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone talking a lot regains the strength of their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice back' is read together: the verb is turned round first, then the power goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk noisily and at length, the same as chattering.

clue.text: Left chosen ground, beginning to seek monster's abode?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their chosen spot to go searching for a beast's lair.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the lake is home to the legendary Nessie.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Ness, a Scottish lake, is the reputed home of the legendary Loch Ness Monster, nicknamed Nessie.
